text.p: Italian bonds and futures continued their positive tone seen in the past four sessions and closed firmer, but off session highs, boosted by the firmer lira tracking the strong dollar and with the market more optimistic over the country's key 1997 budget, traders said.
One said the market was seeing active buying by both Italian and foreign investors. In the afternoon, prices came off highs on profit-taking in reaction to the recent days' gains.
"The climate has changed to being favourable again for high-yielders. The best performing markets today have been Italy and Spain," one trader noted.
Dealers were still fairly sanguine over the 1997 budget which the government of centre-left Prime Minister Romano Prodi hopes to present to parliament by the end of September.

Fausto Bertinotti, leader of the hard-left Communist Refoundation party, said on Monday he had a useful meeting with Prodi on the budget but said they still had differences over the package which aims to cut 1997's PSBR by 32.4 trillion lire.
"A meeting between these two certainly isn't enough to think that the government's partners might have suddenly resolved all their problems," one trader said.
One said the market's positive sentiment was helped by the Bank of Italy's more relaxed policy on the interbank market.
